stem.text: Stomata have daily rhythms of opening and closing. Stomatal aperture width and the concentration of potassium ions in guard cells were measured in the leaves of basil plants, Ocimum basilicum. The basil plants were grown in conditions of natural light, with optimum temperature and soil moisture.
Figure 3.1 shows the results obtained between the times of 06:00 and 17:00. Error bars have been included.

stem.caption: Figure 3.1
stem.alt: Daily changes in stomatal aperture width and potassium ion concentration in basil guard cells, with error bars.

stem.text: With reference to Figure 3.1, describe the changes that occur in mean stomatal aperture width and suggest reasons why these changes benefit basil plants.

guidance: ALLOW mp 3 either in context of 3a or 3b but not twice
3b ALLOW in dark / at night / before 06.00, no photosynthesis
4 ECF from mp 1 if peak time or width wrong

points.text: width increases from 1 to 6.5 mm between 06.00 and 11.00 ;
so (more) carbon dioxide can, enter / diffuse in ;
3a high / rising, light intensity → high / more, photosynthesis ; (afternoon / night / closing / width decreasing, context)
3b low / decreasing, light intensity → low / less, photosynthesis ;
width decreases from 6.5 to 3 mm between 11.00 and 17.00 ;
to, decrease / limit, transpiration / water loss ;

explanation.text: Opening stomata increases carbon dioxide access but also increases water loss. Interpret both phases of the daily trace as a balance between photosynthetic opportunity and conservation of water.

reasoningChain: Quote the morning increase and afternoon decrease with times.
Explain the benefit of each change in its light conditions.

stem.text: Figure 3.1 shows there is a correlation between mean stomatal aperture width and the concentration of potassium ions in guard cells.
Explain how a change in one of these factors may cause a change in the other factor.

points.text: water enters cell, by osmosis / down water potential gradient→ increase in volume / increase in turgor / cell becomes turgid ;
action in mp 1 or 2 causally linked to: widens aperture / opens stoma(ta) ;

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: Potassium uptake lowers guard-cell water potential. Osmotic water uptake increases turgor, and the uneven wall structure converts this volume increase into widening of the pore.

reasoningChain: Trace potassium uptake to a fall in water potential.
Link osmosis and guard-cell turgor to aperture widening.

stem.text: Researchers observed a daily rhythm in the synthesis of abscisic acid (ABA) in plants.
Suggest whether ABA concentration is more likely to increase when light intensity is increasing or is more likely to increase when light intensity is decreasing.

markScheme.instruction: any three from: ABA concentration is more likely to increase when light intensity is decreasing because:
guidance: If answer is about when ABA will decrease (not answering question), CON 1 mark then apply ECF after first error
If answer states that ABA rises when light intensity is increasing, CON 1 mark then apply ECF after first error

points.text: ABA stops H+ moving, out of cell / into cell wall ;
(ABA)causes Ca2+ ions to enter, cytoplasm / cell ;
(ABA)leads to, water leaving (cell) / guard cell becoming flaccid / stomatal closing ;

explanation.text: ABA signalling promotes calcium entry into the cytoplasm and potassium loss from guard cells. Water then leaves by osmosis, reducing turgor and favouring stomatal closure.

reasoningChain: Choose the light trend consistent with stomatal closure.
Connect ABA signalling to ion movement, water movement and reduced aperture.
